full_judgment:
32. Mr. Mostafa Kamal in support of his argument has referred to the following rulings : 26 D.L.R. 285, Rahimuddin Ahmed Vs. Bengal Waterways Ltd.; A.I.R. 1933 Lah. 301, In Re The Punjab Flying Club Ltd. A.I.R. 1936 P.C. 114, D. Davis V. Brunswick; A.I.R. 1941 Pat. 603, Sudhiya Nath Bhaduri Vs. Bihar National Insurance Co. Ltd. Patna; A.I.R. 1959 Trtpura 41, Tripura Administration Vs. Tripura State Bank; A.I.R. 1950 East Punjab 142, M/S. Vanaspati Industries Ltd. Vs. Firm Prabhu Dayal Hari Ram; A.I.R. 1942 Bom. 231, In re Cine Industries & Recording Co. Ltd. ; 17 D.L.R. (S.C.) 52, Shri Ladhi Prashad Jaiswal Vs. The Karnal Distillary Co. Ltd.; (1935), Inch. D. 693, Re Davis & Collect Ltd.; (1916) 2 Ch. D. 426, In re Yenidje Tobacco Co. Ltd., Halsbury's Laws of England, (3rd Edn.), Vol. VI, p. 533 and 535; Buckley on Companies Act, 11th Edn. page 364-365. 

 41. In A.I.R. 1950 East Punjab 142, Messrs Vanaspati Industries Ltd. vs. Firm Prabhu Dayal Hari Ram, winding up petition was filed by the creditors on two grounds, namely, (1) inability to pay debts and that (2) it was just and equitable to wind up the Company. It was found that the Co. was heavily indebted to various creditors and all its assets are in mortgage or in pledge and there 'was no' chance of its being able to carry on its business.
